solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secret identity masking expression of disgust by Catholic female

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: something masking another covers it up, so these letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as on an ID card
fie is an old exclamation of disgust or outrage

explanation.surface: Someone's secret identity hides their disgust with a Catholic woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are restricted ones, kept secret from the public.

clue.text: Start of crossword takes a long time in 3D grid

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an age is a very long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: A solver complains that starting the crossword takes forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is a structure of bars crossing in three dimensions, a grid with depth.

clue.text: Shake up tie with star performer

indicators.note: to shake up a set of letters is to jumble them into a new order

explanation.surface: A style tip: rumple your tie to look like a star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, a singer or dancer on stage.

clue.text: Get off your backside, perhaps? That could help pay the bills

definitions.meaning: a command to rise to your feet is literally an instruction to be upright

definitions.text: That could help pay the bills
definitions.meaning: a regular bank instruction that pays a fixed sum to someone at set intervals

explanation.surface: A nagging partner tells a layabout to get up and earn some money.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank mandate for repeated fixed payments settles regular bills; read literally it is a command to get up.

clue.text: Fool, oddly obstinate and single-minded

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word before it

parts.note: cussed means stubborn and awkward

explanation.surface: A description of a stubborn fool with a one-track mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A focused person concentrates on one aim, which is what single-minded means.

clue.text: Trouble tracking letter? Try this instead

definitions.text: Trouble tracking letter? Try this instead

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so this piece comes second

parts.note: em is the spelt-out name of the letter M
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Advice to someone whose posted letter has gone astray: use electronic mail instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracking' looks like tracing a lost parcel, but it means following. The whole clue doubles as the definition, offering the alternative to a postal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic messages replace postal letters, avoiding the trouble of tracing one lost in the post.

clue.text: Vegetable fat turned into hummus ingredient

indicators.note: turned means the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a spread made from vegetable fat

explanation.surface: A cook's mishap: vegetable fat accidentally ends up in the hummus.
explanation.definitionFit: Gram is another name for the chickpea, the pulse from which hummus is made.

clue.text: Staggering fish caught by group

indicators.note: being caught by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: An amazing fish has been landed by a party of anglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like 'astonishing' describing the catch, but it means tottering.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling means lurching or swaying unsteadily, just as staggering does.

clue.text: Cruelly toying with miss — he doesn't like her

indicators.note: the letters are treated cruelly, twisted out of their order

explanation.surface: A man cruelly plays with a woman's feelings because he dislikes her.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman-hater dislikes women in general, so he does not like her.

clue.text: 'Must be off, bye-bye' — first one leaves

parts.note: go means leave, as in 'be off with you'

indicators.note: one is A, and the first A of the word is removed

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal British farewell

explanation.surface: Someone excuses themself, saying they must go, as the first guest departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotta is a casual spoken form of 'have got to', meaning must.

clue.text: Unattractive Conservative presenting no threat

parts.note: harmless means posing no danger

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is dull but at least not dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking appeal or charm is unattractive.

clue.text: One coming to class late unfortunately met us and truanted

indicators.note: the letters have suffered misfortune and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A latecomer bumped into us and skipped class altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like tardiness, but it means late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult who returns to education later in life is a student who comes to class late.

clue.text: Left or Right finding division bell's sound hilarious

parts.note: left and right are each a side
a split is a division
ting is the light ringing noise of a small bell

explanation.surface: Politicians of left or right find the parliamentary division bell very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The division bell rings in the UK Parliament to call members to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-splitting describes laughter so violent it feels as if your sides might burst.

clue.text: I make type of mixture with gold, incorporating iodine

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of another word

parts.note: compost is a mixture of decayed matter, and also a general word for a mixture
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A recipe: a type of mixture with gold and a dash of iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I make type' is the definition, cleverly running into 'of mixture'.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor sets up printing type, the person who assembles letters for printing.

clue.text: Note: nine at variance with such?

definitions.text: Note: nine at variance with such?

indicators.note: letters at variance with their usual order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like observation about odds and the number nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble of NOTE and NINE gives the answer, and the clue hints that the odds of nine being at variance are slim.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio of one out of every ten, the sort of odds against which nine of the ten differ.

clue.text: Keep breathing smoke? He will

parts.note: read as a smoker's instruction to carry on puffing, and as the fire-breathing creature who always does

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a smoker will keep puffing, and is told he will.
explanation.walkthrough: To drag on a cigarette is to inhale its smoke, so 'keep breathing smoke' splits as DRAG ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical fire-breathing monster of legend exhales smoke and flame.

clue.text: Scots tut, volume 26 turning up inside vault

indicators.note: inside means these letters are placed within the word that follows

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of irritation

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the answer to clue 26, which means unusual

explanation.surface: A Scotsman tuts at a volume, ending up inside a vault.
explanation.definitionFit: To overarch is to form an arch over something, as a vaulted roof does.

clue.text: Thought leader going to practise arms control?

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and going means it is removed

parts.note: an opinion is a thought or view

explanation.surface: An opinion leader is about to support disarmament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms control' suggests weapons treaties, but it means literally restraining someone's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinion someone is to bind or hold their arms so they cannot move them.

clue.text: I wouldn't fancy this Japanese drama, musical one with no acting

parts.note: Noh is a classical form of Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: with no means leaving out the next piece

parts.note: an opera is a musical work
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a rank title

explanation.surface: A theatregoer is unimpressed by a Japanese play that is all music and no acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like 'like', but in betting to fancy a runner is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a competitor with no chance of winning, one a punter would not back.

clue.text: Excuses when getting one's visa processed

indicators.note: processed means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats make excuses when someone's visa is being processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasions are dodges or pretexts used to avoid the truth, much like excuses.

clue.text: Continent regularly touches another to the north rather than south

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

indicators.text: to the north rather than south
indicators.note: N for north replaces S for south

parts.note: another continent, here Asia

explanation.surface: One continent borders another, lying to its north rather than its south.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region of Australia and the Pacific islands, often counted as a continent.

clue.text: Collapse of shared fence around upland borders causing unneighbourly feeling?

indicators.note: a collapse breaks the letters down and rebuilds them in another order
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shared fence falls on a hillside, souring relations next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Schadenfreude is pleasure at another's misfortune, an unkind feeling toward those next door.

clue.text: 18's situation, recently arrived?

definitions.meaning: the position of a hopeless contender who cannot come out on top
newly in stock or in season, as a shop sign might say

explanation.surface: A description of the hopeless one's predicament on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation offers no chance of success; 'now in' announces freshly delivered goods.

clue.text: In place of depravity, get a grip

definitions.meaning: the Latin preposition meaning instead of
a workshop clamp holds things tight; spelt this way in British English

explanation.surface: A stern warning to someone sliding into wickedness: pull yourself together.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: Latin for 'instead of', wickedness, and the bench clamp that grips work.

clue.text: Posh old master?

definitions.meaning: upper-class or of the highest quality
a leading painter of earlier times, read as an artist at the very top

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an upper-class gentleman is a former schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest social class; a top drawer is also a supreme draughtsman.

clue.text: It's boring being cornered by rotten nuisance

indicators.note: the letters are trapped within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Being pinned in a corner by a horrible pest is tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weary listless boredom, the feeling something tedious causes.

clue.text: Unusual to see texting abbreviation followed by its translation

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after

parts.note: in text messages the letter R stands for the word 'are'
the abbreviation spelt out in full

explanation.surface: It is odd to see a text abbreviation with its meaning written beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon or seldom found, a synonym for unusual.

clue.text: China tea's brewed? About time then!

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the next piece
brewed means the letters are stewed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone waiting for their China tea to brew exclaims that it's about time.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In that case' and 'then' both introduce a consequence: if so, then.
